title: Brands We Know
intro: We do not sell every brand on this page, and we are not locked to any of them. These are products and platforms we like working with, and we think they are worth considering for your project. Hover or tap a logo to see why.
footerNote: Brand names and logos are trademarks of their respective owners. We show them because we like working with these products. One Day Systems is not a partner, reseller or certified representative for any brand listed here.

brands.name: QSC Audio
brands.blurb: For gyms, chapels and multipurpose rooms, QSC speakers are a workhorse we trust to sound clear without baby-sitting them.

brands.name: Electro-Voice
brands.blurb: We like how Electro-Voice holds up in loud spaces. Gyms, stages and outdoor events are where this brand earns its keep.

brands.name: Community (loudspeakers)
brands.blurb: Community speakers are built for big rooms and rough weather. Stadiums, parks and school fields are their sweet spot.

brands.name: SoundTube
brands.blurb: A Kansas City-area neighbor. SoundTube ceiling and landscape speakers disappear into the room and still sound great.

brands.name: Meyer Sound
brands.blurb: When the room has to sound right the first time, Meyer Sound is the premium pick. Support and consistency are a big part of why we like them.

brands.name: Allen & Heath
brands.blurb: We like how Allen & Heath mixers stay friendly under pressure. Live events and worship spaces get a desk that operators actually enjoy.

brands.name: Yamaha
brands.blurb: Yamaha desks and install mixers are familiar to almost every tech. Reliable, widely supported, and easy to hand off.

brands.name: Midas
brands.blurb: For stages that want that classic console feel, Midas still delivers. Warm, solid and built for live sound.

brands.name: Audix
brands.blurb: We like Audix for stages and pulpits. Tough mics that sound honest and do not need constant fussing.

brands.name: Shure
brands.blurb: A safe choice for boardrooms, gyms and event stages alike. Shure just works, and support is easy to find.

brands.name: Earthworks Audio
brands.blurb: When the table needs to disappear and voices still cut through, Earthworks ceiling and boundary mics shine.

brands.name: Visionary Solutions
brands.blurb: We like how Visionary keeps video on the network simple. Clean AV-over-IP that fits modern classrooms and conference rooms.

brands.name: Covid, Inc. (AV)
brands.blurb: The quiet heroes in the rack. Covid wall plates, cables and extenders keep rooms tidy and signal paths boring in the best way.

brands.name: Comprehensive Cable
brands.blurb: Good cable is invisible until it fails. Comprehensive is a practical, widely stocked choice we reach for on everyday installs.

brands.name: AVPro Edge
brands.blurb: Midwest-made switching and distribution. AVPro Edge fits when you want solid HDMI and HDBaseT gear without drama.

brands.name: Hall Research
brands.blurb: Hall Research makes the dependable, US-built extenders, splitters and switchers that get a clean picture from the rack to the screen across the room or across the building, without fuss.

brands.name: Samsung Direct View LED
brands.blurb: When a lobby or chapel needs a true LED canvas, Samsung direct-view walls look sharp and stay serviceable.

brands.name: Absen
brands.blurb: Absen LED walls show up in houses of worship and venues that want bright, scalable displays at a fair price.

brands.name: Q-SYS (QSC)
brands.blurb: Audio, video and control on one platform. Q-SYS keeps bigger rooms simpler to run day to day.

brands.name: Biamp
brands.blurb: We like Biamp when people need to be heard clearly. Dependable conferencing audio for rooms that matter.

brands.name: Epson
brands.blurb: Classroom projectors that hold up well for the price. Epson is a familiar, easy-to-support choice.

brands.name: Samsung
brands.blurb: Commercial displays for lobbies, signage and conference rooms. Steady picture and parts you can actually get.

brands.name: Sony
brands.blurb: When a room needs a step up in picture or a solid PTZ camera, Sony pro gear is a safe bet.

brands.name: Logitech
brands.blurb: Simple room kits that are easy on the budget. Great for small huddle rooms where anyone can walk up and join.

brands.name: Poly (HP)
brands.blurb: Familiar video bars and conference phones that play nicely with Teams and Zoom. Office-ready and widely supported.

brands.name: Neat
brands.blurb: All-in-one room devices that feel friendly. Walk up, tap, and you are in the meeting.

brands.name: Legrand AV (Chief, Vaddio, Middle Atlantic)
brands.blurb: Mounts, PTZ cameras and racks that hold a good room together. The unglamorous gear that makes everything else behave.

brands.name: VOD Visual North America
brands.blurb: LED walls with local North American support. A practical path when a space needs a big, bright canvas.

brands.name: NETGEAR AV
brands.blurb: For AV-over-IP networks, NETGEAR's AV switches are pre-tuned for media. Less fiddling, more content on the wall.

brands.name: Cisco
brands.blurb: The standard in a lot of districts and larger offices. Knowing Cisco well helps us support what you already have.

brands.name: Cisco Meraki
brands.blurb: Cloud-managed Wi-Fi and switching a small IT team can run from one dashboard after we hand it off.

brands.name: HPE Aruba Networking
brands.blurb: Strong campus Wi-Fi for schools and offices with a lot of devices. Built for dense, busy networks.

brands.name: Extreme Networks
brands.blurb: Common in K-12 and a solid choice at a fair price. Extreme gives districts another path that still feels enterprise.

brands.name: Ubiquiti (UniFi)
brands.blurb: Good value Wi-Fi and switching when the budget is tight. UniFi can cover a small business or building without breaking the bank.

brands.name: Cambium Networks
brands.blurb: Useful for linking buildings and reaching rural sites where fiber is hard to get. Outdoor wireless done thoughtfully.

brands.name: Sophos
brands.blurb: Firewall and endpoint protection that is easier to keep up with. A practical stack for schools and mid-size offices.

brands.name: Palo Alto Networks
brands.blurb: Top-shelf next-gen firewalls. May be more than most clients need, but when the bar is high, this is the name.

brands.name: Axis Communications
brands.blurb: Well-built cameras that work with almost any video system. Open, reliable and a favorite for long-lived installs.

brands.name: Avigilon (Motorola Solutions)
brands.blurb: Smarter search and alerts on video. Strong when a site wants cameras that help staff find what matters faster.

brands.name: Bosch Security
brands.blurb: A long-trusted name in building security. Many facilities already know Bosch, which makes upgrades smoother.

brands.name: Eagle Eye Networks
brands.blurb: Cloud VMS that can move existing cameras online without replacing everything. Practical path to modern video.

brands.name: HALO Smart Sensor
brands.blurb: Schools ask about vape and air-quality detection a lot. HALO is a common, clear answer we are glad to support.

brands.name: Brivo
brands.blurb: Cloud access that works for one door or many sites. Established, steady and easy for staff to live with.

brands.name: Avigilon Alta (formerly Openpath)
brands.blurb: Phone-based entry that feels modern. Alta makes coming and going simple for staff without a pile of plastic cards.

brands.name: LenelS2
brands.blurb: Fits larger campuses and government buildings with many doors. Enterprise access when the site is complex.

brands.name: Genetec Synergis
brands.blurb: Access control that lives inside Genetec. Makes sense when cameras and doors should share one system.

brands.name: HID Global
brands.blurb: Readers and cards found in a lot of buildings. We work with HID often because so many doors already speak it.

brands.name: Allegion (Schlage)
brands.blurb: Schlage hardware is a common, dependable choice for doors in schools and offices. Locks people already trust.

brands.name: ASSA ABLOY
brands.blurb: Much of the door hardware access control depends on. Exit devices and strikes that keep openings code-right.

brands.name: Microsoft Teams Phone
brands.blurb: Calling inside the Microsoft world you already use. Natural fit for places that live in Microsoft 365.

brands.name: Zoom Phone
brands.blurb: Cloud calling for organizations that already meet on Zoom. One familiar app for meetings and desk calls.

brands.name: Webex Calling (Cisco)
brands.blurb: Cloud calling that fits sites already on Cisco gear. Familiar, enterprise-ready and well supported.

brands.name: Mitel
brands.blurb: Many schools and offices still run Mitel. Helping with upgrades from it is part of how we keep phone systems calm.

brands.name: AtlasIED
brands.blurb: School paging, bells and speakers. AtlasIED is a common, trusted choice in education buildings.

brands.name: Valcom
brands.blurb: Simple paging that has lived in schools and warehouses for years. Straightforward and serviceable.

brands.name: Algo Communication Products
brands.blurb: SIP paging speakers and strobes that drop cleanly onto a VoIP phone system. Easy alerts without a separate island.

brands.name: Singlewire InformaCast
brands.blurb: Ties phones, speakers and screens together for lockdowns and alerts. Midwest-made mass notification done right.

brands.name: Dell Technologies
brands.blurb: Common, dependable staff computers and small servers. Easy to buy, easy to support, easy to replace parts for.

brands.name: HP
brands.blurb: Familiar to most offices and schools. Laptops, desktops and printers with support you can actually reach.

brands.name: Lenovo
brands.blurb: ThinkPads and Chromebooks that hold up well for staff and students. A volume choice in a lot of classrooms.

brands.name: Apple
brands.blurb: Macs and iPads show up in plenty of schools. We plan networks and rooms so they feel at home.

brands.name: Google Chromebooks (ChromeOS)
brands.blurb: Chromebooks are everywhere in K-12. They need good Wi-Fi, and we build for that.

brands.name: Microsoft 365 / Teams / Teams Rooms
brands.blurb: The backbone for many of our clients. Rooms and networks get built around the Microsoft world people already live in.

brands.name: Google Workspace (for Education)
brands.blurb: Many schools run on Google. We make sure rooms and devices fit Classroom, Meet and the rest without friction.

brands.name: Zoom (Workplace / Rooms)
brands.blurb: Zoom Rooms are a common conference-room choice, and lots of gear supports them cleanly.

brands.name: Cisco Webex
brands.blurb: Meetings and room devices for organizations already on Cisco. Familiar stack, familiar support path.

brands.name: Jamf
brands.blurb: Keeps iPads and Macs managed. Matters a lot in schools with carts full of Apple devices.

brands.name: Microsoft Intune
brands.blurb: Helps keep staff computers updated and secure without a lot of hands-on work. Quiet, useful device management.

brands.name: Switchcraft
brands.blurb: Chicago-made connectors and panels. The little parts that keep a rack honest for years.

brands.name: Neutrik
brands.blurb: SpeakON, XLR and etherCON done right. Neutrik connectors are what we reach for when a cable has to survive the road.

brands.name: Radio Design Labs (RDL)
brands.blurb: RDL sticks and modules solve the odd little audio problems. Compact, dependable and made for integrators.

brands.name: Lowell Manufacturing
brands.blurb: Racks, panels and power the quiet Midwestern way. Lowell keeps closets neat so the next tech has an easier day.

brands.name: Panduit
brands.blurb: Cabling pieces that keep a closet neat and easy to work in. Small details that save hours later.

brands.name: CommScope (SYSTIMAX)
brands.blurb: Copper and fiber systems common in larger buildings that want a long warranty on the wiring.

brands.name: Leviton
brands.blurb: Practical, widely available network jacks and panels. Everyday wiring done without drama.

brands.name: Chatsworth Products
brands.blurb: Racks and cabinets that keep network closets organized and safe. The frame everything else hangs on.

brands.name: APC by Schneider Electric
brands.blurb: Battery backups that keep networks and phones running through short power blips. Peace of mind in a rack unit.
